ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against Financial Intelligence Centre (FIC) sanctions lists, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and South African domestic POCDATARA lists prior to incorporation. PEP identification required on a risk-based basis; enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs, immediate family and close associates; screening must cover all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and signatories at inception and on any change. Compliance with FIC Guidance Note 4A: Guidance for accountable institutions on Section 28E and Section 28C obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) eServices portal – https://www.cipc.co.za
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be expressed in any of the 11 official South African languages or English, but must be rendered in the Latin alphabet. The name must be easily pronounceable, must not mislead on the nature of the business, and must include a legal form suffix ('(Pty) Ltd'). Non-Latin script trade names or brand translations must be applied for separately as company name alternatives in a Latin transliteration. Arabic, Mandarin, Hindi or other non-Latin characters are generally not accepted for the registered legal name; the safe practice is to file a Latinised transliteration.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Name rejection is communicated electronically via CIPC eServices with a reason code. An applicant may apply for reconsideration through the CIPC Name and Trading Name Objection system within 10 business days of rejection. If unreseved via administrative appeal, the applicant may file Form CoR 9.5 'Notice of Renewal of a Reservation of a Company Name' for one additional 6-month period. If the name remains rejected on substantive grounds (e.g., confusing similarity or prohibited token), a formal objection may be filed under sections 160-161 of Companies Act 71 of 2008, followed by referral to the Companies Tribunal within 15 business days. If the Companies Tribunal decision is unfavourable, judicial review before the High Court of South Africa is available on a 180-day window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a retail grocery business, virtual offices are not fully permissive for actual trading premises. A physical business premises license under municipal business regulations and food retail licensing (e.g., Grocery Store License / Certificate of Compliance under National Health Act 61 of 2003) is mandatory. A virtual office can be used for statutory registered office postal address, but the physical retail location must be a real place of business and be disclosed to CIPC. The company must retain a registered address in South Africa at a physical location where documents may be served.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderately high (45%–55% probability) within first operational year due to municipal health and safety inspections, food safety compliance (R638 of 2018 regulations), and retail business licensing compliance checks. Unannounced inspections of food retail premises are common for imported Asian condiments and fresh produce.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act 71 of 2008, as amended: sections 13 (incorporated by registration), 14 (registration of incorporation), 15 (Memorandum of Incorporation), 19 (legal personality), and 66 (board of directors)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC), acting under the Department of Trade, Industry and Competition
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Incorporation (Form CoR 14.1A) together with the Memorandum of Incorporation (MOI)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a private company. The MOI may specify authorized shares; no escrow or capital deposit requirement applies to an ordinary private retail company.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED that each subscriber to the Memorandum of Incorporation hereby subscribes for the number of shares set opposite his or her name, with the aggregate subscription monies paid into the company's designated bank account. RESOLVED that the premises situated at [registered address] are adopted as the registered office of the company. RESOLVED that [Name] is appointed as the sole Director, [Name] as Company Secretary, and [Name] as Financial Officer for the purpose of bank dealings and regulatory filings. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors are authorized to cause incorporation with CIPC, SARS, and municipal licensing authorities and to execute all documents necessary to commence lawful supermarket trading.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Login to CIPC e-Services, complete and submit the Company Name Reservation application (Form CoR 9.1), pay the prescribed fee, and await approval of a name number valid for six months. The name must be distinguishable from existing registered names.
required_dossiers: Proof of identity of each incorporator
Power of attorney if an agent acts on behalf of incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, opposed, or resembles an existing name, submit a supplementary name reservation with alternative distinctive names and provide written reasons distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting entities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting of Incorporation Documents and Consents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: CIPC, or a registered company secretary or transaction attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum of Incorporation complying with the Companies Act, specifying the share capital structure, directors, and governance rules. Prepare the Notice of Incorporation (CoR 14.1A) and obtain signed director consents.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (CoR 14.1B equivalent)
Certified copies of directors' identity documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CIPC flags formatting or content defects, amend the relevant schedule and resubmit with a formal response letter within the same filing cycle.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Notice of Incorporation and MOI electronically, pay the registration fee, and track the application using the issued filing reference number. Upon approval, download the Certificate of Incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond in writing within the permitted period, provide corrected documents, and pay any re-filing fee. If rejected, file an administrative appeal with CIPC within 20 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and Employer Registration with SARS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS) via eFiling or SARS branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for income tax, VAT (compulsory if annual turnover exceeds the R1 million threshold), PAYE if employing staff, and obtain a tax clearance number. Provide bank account confirmation and company registration details.
required_dossiers: SARS tax registration form (e.g. form RPI001)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SARS rejects or queries the application, correct the CIT or VAT registration details and resubmit; escalate to a SARS branch consultant for manual processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Employment and Labour (DEL) - Unemployment Insurance Fund and Compensation Fund
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company as an employer for the Unemployment Insurance Fund (UIF) and under the Compensation for Occupational Injuries and Diseases Act (COIDA). Obtain the employer number and ensure workmen's compensation compliance before staff commence duties.
required_dossiers: Bank and contact details of the company
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registration is delayed or findings are raised, respond through the DEL online portal or local labour centre; submit outstanding payroll data and clarify worker classification to prevent penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: National Department of Health and the applicable Metropolitan Municipality licensing office (e.g. City of Johannesburg or City of Cape Town)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Certificate of Acceptability for food premises issued under the Foodstuffs, Cosmetics and Disinfectants Act, 1972, and a Business (Trading) Licence under the municipal business by-laws

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no formal environmental impact assessment required for small-scale grocery retail premises not listed under Listing Notice 1 or 2 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Regulations, 2014
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater must comply with municipal sewer by-law discharge limits and the National Water Act; no significant VOC emissions expected, but storage of cleaning agents must be controlled; solid waste must be separated and collected in accordance with the National Environmental Management: Waste Act, 2008 and municipal waste regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the municipal fire protection authority confirming emergency exits, fire extinguishers, and safe occupant load; structural load clearance from a registered professional engineer for racking and cold storage areas; occupational health and safety compliance clearance under the Occupational Health and Safety Act 85 of 1993 for the retail floor and back-of-house areas.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: South African Revenue Service (SARS); national self-assessment portal: SARS eFiling (https://www.sarsefiling.co.za); entity incorporation and company registry: Companies and Intellectual Property Commission (CIPC) portal (https://www.cipc.co.za); customs clearance: SARS Customs via e@syFile and Asycuda World.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned (Pty) Ltd must first incorporate under the Companies Act 71 of 2008 through CIPC to obtain a company registration number. Thereafter the company registers as a taxpayer with SARS via eFiling to obtain an income tax reference number (IT number), and, upon exceeding or expecting to exceed the VAT threshold, files the VAT 101 application to obtain a VAT vendor number. A foreign entity not locally incorporated but making taxable supplies in South Africa may register directly for VAT (and PAYE if applicable) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991, supplying proof of non-resident status and appointing a SARS-recognized representative vendor. Non-resident shareholding is permitted and no minimum capital is required. A municipal business licence (Business Act 71 of 1991) is required before trading.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a South Africa-incorporated (Pty) Ltd is a tax resident company taxed at 27% normal tax on worldwide income (years of assessment ending on or after 31 March 2023); no pass-through eligibility and no tax-exempt zone status; distributions are subject to 20% dividends tax at shareholder level.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election; classification is statutory. Available elections relevant to this entity: (1) VAT grouping election under s.50 of the VAT Act for closely linked entities; (2) voluntary VAT registration election once annual taxable turnover reaches ZAR 50,000; (3) foreign hybrid entity election under s.25B(2A) of the Income Tax Act 58 of 1962 for a foreign entity treated as a company in its residence jurisdiction; (4) anti-hybrid rule elections under s.23K of the Income Tax Act; (5) CFC elections and participation-exemption elections for foreign subsidiaries. All elections must be submitted to SARS within prescribed statutory timeframes via eFiling.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act 89 of 1991
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Compulsory registration: ZAR 1,000,000 annual taxable turnover (s.23(1) VAT Act); voluntary registration: ZAR 50,000 annual taxable turnover (s.23(2)); foreign suppliers of electronic services: compulsory registration under s.23A with no threshold. Imported goods are subject to VAT at 15% at customs, with the importer claiming an input tax deduction on receipt of the customs release documentation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping mandate is in force; SARS is deploying a Continuous Transaction Controls (CTC) e-invoicing pilot (SARS eInvoicing, PEPPOL-based) with voluntary participation pending gazetted mandatory timelines. Current mandates: a full tax invoice under s.20 of the VAT Act must be issued within 21 days of a taxable supply to a VAT vendor, containing prescribed particulars (vendor name and VAT number, invoice number, date, description, quantity, consideration, VAT amount, and VAT rate); abridged tax invoices are permissible for supplies up to ZAR 5,000 including VAT. POS terminals must be configured to issue SARS-compliant tax invoices because retail sales to consumers are final supplies; no fiscal device registration is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies under s.11(1)(a) of the VAT Act where movable goods are supplied to a non-resident and physically exported from South Africa within 90 days of supply (extension possible for unavoidable delays). Cross-border consignment sales of packaged Asian grocery products qualify if proof of physical removal is retained. Services rendered to non-residents that are not supplied for use in South Africa qualify under s.11(2)(l). Ordinary in-store retail sales at POS terminals within the Republic are taxable at 15% and cannot be zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (SAD 500) lodged via SARS Customs (e@syFile/Asycuda World) reflecting HS codes, gross mass, and export justification
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical departure from a South African port or airport
VAT 264 export certificate (where requested by SARS) and the supplier's full tax invoice or abridged tax invoice
Proof of foreign consideration: inward remittance certificate or bank foreign-exchange confirmation in compliance with Exchange Control Regulation 6
Supporting transport and insurance documents (CMR waybill, container receipt, packing list) corroborating the export movement
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: SARS Export Verification Unit cross-matches SAD 500 declarations, cargo manifests, bank forex receipts, and VAT 264 certificates. A false or unsupported zero-rating claim triggers additional VAT assessed under s.66 of the VAT Act plus interest (s.39 Tax Administration Act) and an understatement penalty of 10% to 150% of the shortfall under s.223 of the Tax Administration Act depending on culpability (substantial understatement, no reasonable grounds, gross negligence, or intentional evasion). Fraudulent conduct is criminally prosecutable under s.74B of the VAT Act and s.235 of the Tax Administration Act, with fines of up to ZAR 30,000 and/or imprisonment of up to 24 months per offence; refunds are clawed back retrospectively and directors may be held personally liable under s.20 of the Tax Administration Act. Failure to receive export proceeds within 180 days attracts exchange-control penalties and potential prosecution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: South African Reserve Bank (SARB), acting through its Financial Surveillance Department (FinSurv), under the Currency and Exchanges Act 9 of 1933, the Exchange Control Manual (as revised), and the Financial Intelligence Centre Act 38 of 2001 (FICA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The South African rand (ZAR) is freely usable for genuine current-account flows (imports, services, salaries, interest, dividends and branch profits) without prior FinSurv approval, but every remittance must be routed through an Authorised Dealer (AD) bank in South Africa with full documentary support. Capital-account flows remain administered: inbound equity subscriptions by non-residents are permitted through the AD banking system without the former loop-structure consent, but must be declared on the AD's Balance of Payments (BOP) returns and linked to an EM-code/INPF inward-transfer record so that future dividend and capital repatriations can be matched. Outward capital flows (offshore treasury accounts, loans to connected foreign parties, outward investments) generally require FinSurv approval or a clearly delegated AD consent. In practical terms, dividend/profit remittances are encumbered less by convertibility than by documentation integrity: the AD will require a valid SARS tax clearance (tax compliance status) for foreign remittance, audited or management-account reserve calculations, INPF/EM evidence that the original investment was brought into South Africa through the banking system, and CRS/FATCA self-certifications of the non-resident shareholder. As the entity's business is an Asian-specialty grocery importer/retailer, ZAR sales receipts convert naturally; the residual convertibility friction is confined to validating import payables and maintaining compliant FCA balances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There is currently no fixed mandatory conversion (surrender) percentage for export proceeds; the historical partial-surrender regime was liberalised so that exporters may retain 100% of foreign export receipts in a Foreign Currency Account (FCA) held with an Authorised Dealer. The operative statutory and compliance obligations are: (i) the full export value must be received within 180 days from the date of shipment unless FinSurv has approved a longer period; (ii) proceeds must be brought into South Africa's banking system by being credited to an FCA or converted to ZAR through an AD; (iii) every receipt must be supported by the SAD500 bill of entry, commercial invoice, transport document and proof of shipment. If the entity re-exports goods or earns fees from cross-border marketing, the same 180-day repatriation rule applies. Failure to repatriate or offering proceeds to an unauthorised foreign account is an exchange-control contravention exposing the company and responsible directors to administrative penalties and criminal liability under the Currency and Exchanges Act.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium as a supplementary payment-instruction utility, but Low as the principal treasury clearing rail for a South African resident company. South African exchange-control rules require residents to route all cross-border receipts and payments through an Authorised Dealer incorporated in South Africa; an offshore digital EMI (e.g., Wise Business, Revolut Business, Payoneer) cannot hold or operate the company's foreign-currency cash pool in substitution for a SARB-regulated FCA. Using an offshore EMI to park trade collections or to fund suppliers outside the AD channel would constitute unapproved retention/acquisition of foreign currency and would expose the company to FinSurv penalties, adverse findings on the next AD audit, and difficulty in evidencing the EM-code trail for future dividend remittances. Lawful limited use: the company may designate the EMI account of a non-resident supplier as the beneficiary of an MT103/OPC payment originated by the AD; supplier-side fintech receipts do not affect the SA treasury structure. The recommended posture is to operate via a major AD (Standard Bank, FNB, Absa or Nedbank) with FCA and direct SWIFT coverage into Asia and to avoid any offshore bulk-funding or collections aggregation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: All banks apply FICA-compliant customer due diligence. Resident directors may, in most of the four major banks, complete onboarding remotely through liveness-verified digital identity (linked to the Department of Home Affairs and CIPC databases) followed by a recorded video compliance interview; nonetheless, first account activation frequently requires at least one resident signatory to attend a branch in person to execute the mandate. Non-resident directors (e.g., shareholder-appointed representatives in Asia) need not be physically present if they provide notarised/apostilled passports, CIPC or foreign registry extracts, source-of-funds declarations, FATCA/CRS self-certifications and attend a video interview; banks may additionally require the South African compliance officer to witness the board resolution approving the mandate. Exchanging the physical-visit requirement for an expedited video path is bank-by-bank discretionary and conditional on risk grading; the safest programme is to fly the CFO or an authorised local director to the chosen bank's Johannesburg, Cape Town or Durban corporate branch for a single half-day signing and interview session, which reduces onboarding from 4-8 weeks to 1-2 weeks.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: shareholding held through nominees, offshore trusts, or a non-resident corporate parent without transparent UBO identification.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: CIPC register of members with full legal-name disclosure; entity organogram to natural-person UBO level; notarised/apostilled passports of UBOs; trust deed or parent-company board resolution confirming control; FATCA/CRS self-certifications; signed UBO declaration forms of the relevant bank and confirmations that no politically exposed persons (PEPs) are present.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-risk geographic exposure: Asian supplier corridors (PRC, Hong Kong, Singapore, ASEAN) triggering secondary-Sanctions or country-risk screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative match reports from OFAC/EU/UN consolidated-list screening; supplier business-licence extracts; vendor compliance attestations against U.S./EU/UN sanctions; detailed contract files, end-use and end-beneficiary letters for each edible-goods purchase confirming absence of dual-use applicability; freight-forwarder and customs-broker KYC confirmation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Disproportionate cash and card revenue flows: rapid POS/card and cash deposits inconsistent with a grocery retail turnover profile, raising money-laundering suspicion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Daily POS/EFT terminal reports integrated into the accounting system; daily cash-up and security-transport records; VAT201 declarations and SARS assessment correspondence matching turnover bands; store-level sales journal and inventory purchase invoices; bank statements reconciling tender-type deposits; a written cash-management policy and AML risk assessment approved by the board.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money-laundering indicators: import mispricing, over- or under-invoicing, split shipments or round-tripping in Asian condiment/vegetable imports.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: SAD500 bill of entry per consignment; fully matched commercial invoices and purchase contracts; bill of lading/air waybill and packing lists; independent benchmark pricing for comparable specialty grocery categories; customs warehouse receipting and stock-movement records; insurance certificates and freight invoices; reconciliation of MT103 payment amounts to invoice and customs values.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-compliance red flag: open SARS assessments, cancelled tax-clearance status or VAT/CIT arrears detected during the bank's FICA due-diligence checks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current SARS Tax Compliance Status pin; latest ITR14 and VAT201 submissions and proof of provisional-tax payments; letter of good standing from the registered tax practitioner; schedule of any outstanding payments and agreed SARS payment arrangements; board resolution confirming no tax avoidance structures and full transfer-pricing documentation for related-party supplier invoices.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Related-party cross-border loan or funding without at-arm's-length pricing, triggering thin-capitalisation and exchange-control review of inward loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Inward loan agreement with commercial interest and repayment schedule; transfer-pricing documentation (SARS TP-102/33); market-rate benchmarking (IBOR/SARB reference); FinSurv/AD-approved inward-loan acceptance communicated in writing; BOP 'Other Investment' declaration records; audited financial statements evidencing the use of proceeds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for non-resident shareholder funding: (1) execute the board/shareholder resolutions and CIPC allotment filings; (2) instruct the shareholder's foreign bank to wire funds to the chosen AD-nostro beneficiary account of the company, using a purpose line 'Equity Subscription - [Company Reg. No.]' and the shareholder's tax identification; (3) present to the AD the certification of incorporation, memorandum of incorporation, board resolution, share subscription agreement and control-organisation chart; (4) the AD records the inflow on an INPF/EM-code inward Foreign Direct Investment record and credits either the ZAR ordinary account (post-conversion) or a resident FCA if retention is elected; (5) issue the share certificates and ensure the AD lodges the BOP 'Direct Investment - Equity Capital' entry in the monthly reporting cycle. Shareholder loans should be documented with a signed loan agreement, commercial rate rationale and the AD's inward-loan acceptance to separate 'Other Investment' liabilities from equity. No prior SARB approval is required for a straightforward unlisted equity injection into a non-resident-owned Pty, but the inward transfer evidence (INPF/EM) must be retained permanently because dividend repatriation at exit is permitted only against funds whose inward route has been proven through the AD banking system.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement of Asian supplier payables should use, in order of documentary strength: (i) SWIFT MT103 (OPC) current-account payments from the AD, each matched to purchase order, commercial invoice, packing list and (once shipped) transport document and SAD500 bill of entry; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit issued under UCP600/URC522 (sight or usance 60-120 days) for high-value perishable vegetable and containerised condiment imports, with the AD issuing and the Chinese/SEA supplier bank negotiating or confirming; (iii) Documentary Collections (D/P, D/A) where LC cost is prohibitive; and (iv) SWIFT MT700/MT798 for amendments and standard bank-guarantee instruments. Payments must match the SARS importer code, customs-declared values and approved FCA balance or local ZAR conversion; the entity should centralise daily POS/card receipts through a single treasury bank in the morning and execute supplier wires only after the previous day's receivables have settled, thereby funding import disbursements from operational cash flow and reserving the FCA and an intra-day credit line for timing mismatches. Local clearing rails (BankservAfrica EFT/ACB and PayShap) remain appropriate for rent, salaries and domestic wholesalers, and must be separated from the border-crossing ledger entries to keep the AD audit trail clean.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable forwards (ZAR/USD, ZAR/EUR, ZAR/CNY) matched to documented import-payment due dates and FCA conversion plans
FX swaps and rollover/extension forward contracts aligned to shipment-delay and perishable-goods renegotiation events
Cross-currency swaps with AD approval where long-dated import-financing or inventory-revolving facilities create matched FX and interest exposures
Covered foreign-exchange options (e.g., zero-premium collars and cost-reduction structures) used to protect gross margins on staple Asian groceries

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs): permissible in this structure only as the offshore mirror risk-transferred by the Authorised Dealer against the onshore hedged exposure; the resident company may not deal in speculative NDFs with unlicensed offshore counterparties, as such dealings would breach the AD-conduit and residence-of-contract requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: CIPC Annual Return (company annual return as per Companies Act s. 33; CoR 36.1)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 business days after the anniversary of the company's incorporation date, every year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: R150 late penalty (plus standard fee). Company placed in default after 30 business days; CIPC issues notice of deregistration; administrative strike-off after 2 consecutive years of non-filing; directors may be personally liable for company debts incurred while in default (s. 22).

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (UBO register annual confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Initial filing on incorporation; within 10 business days of any beneficial ownership change; confirmed annually with the CIPC annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update UBO declaration is an offence under the General Laws (AML/CFT) Amendment Act 22 of 2022: compliance notice up to R1,000,000 fine or imprisonment up to 10 years for directors/officers.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statements (AFS) prepared and presented to shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Board of directors / shareholders (no CIPC filing required for private company with Public Interest Score < 100)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the end of the financial year (Companies Act s. 30(4))
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who fail to prepare AFS per applicable accounting framework breach s. 29/30: CIPC compliance notice; offence under s. 214 (fine and/or imprisonment up to 10 years); shareholders may compel delivery via court application.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (ITR14) with financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 12 months after the end of the company's financial year of assessment (SARS issue date may shorten the period)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative non-compliance penalty: R250 per month (turnover < R1m) up to R1,000 per month (turnover R1m-R10m); 10%-20% late payment penalty plus interest (prime rate + 3% daily compound); criminal prosecution for intentional non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if Public Interest Score (PI) > 350; independent review required if PI 100-350 unless AFS internally prepared (then audit required); no audit/review required if PI < 100. PI points: 1 per employee, 1 per R1m turnover, 1 per R1m third-party liabilities, 1 per individual shareholder. Expected PI: 30-60 for a small Asian supermarket grocery, so no compulsory audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS or IFRS for SMEs (South African Statements of GAAP) per Companies Act s. 29; company may voluntarily elect full IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Register of Beneficial Owners must be maintained on site and filed with CIPC at incorporation and within 10 business days of any shareholding/UBO change; the CIPC annual return includes an annual UBO data confirmation (one or more natural persons with effective control or 5%+ beneficial interest must be disclosed).
